title: Software OpenPGP decompression allocates beyond the configured plaintext limit
root_cause_class: the in-process rPGP provider recursively decompresses an attacker-controlled message and collects the complete literal with as_data_vec before decrypt_authenticated_entity applies max_message_bytes or MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES
demonstrated_impact: A valid 179279-byte received OpenPGP/MIME message expanded to 134217728 plaintext bytes, peaked at 213264 KiB RSS versus an 83664 KiB one-MiB control, and was rejected only after allocation. With RLIMIT_AS=180000 KiB the same message aborted on a 33554432-byte allocation.
impact_tier_reason: A remote sender using only the recipient's public key can select decompressed output large enough to kill the main backend process when a software-key user performs the normal read/decrypt action. The message remains available to retrigger. The OpenPGP feature and user interaction narrow reach but are intended ordinary use, not privileged configuration.
exploit_execution_time_source: Fresh-process decryption time of the retained 128 MiB candidate before the post-allocation size rejection; fixture generation and compilation excluded.
regression_test_or_invariant: Software-provider plaintext is read through a sink capped at min(configured max_message_bytes, MAX_DECRYPTED_BYTES)+1, compressed-packet nesting is bounded, over-limit output stops without retaining it, authenticated failure semantics remain fail-closed, and a following ordinary message decrypts successfully.

unintended_behaviors.behavior: the configured plaintext limit is checked only after the complete decompressed literal has been materialized
unintended_behaviors.expected: decompression output is stopped while streaming at the configured plaintext boundary
unintended_behaviors.actual: as_data_vec allocates the entire attacker-selected plaintext before the caller observes its length

composition.unintended_behavior_count_note: A bounded streaming sink in the software provider closes the demonstrated amplification; nesting should be capped in the same decompression-boundary component.
remediation_components: bounded software-provider decompression/output reader with nesting accounting
composition.remediation_component_count_note: The external GnuPG/YubiKey provider already has bounded subprocess output; this component brings the in-process path to the same invariant.
defense_in_depth: run all cryptographic MIME processing in a disposable resource-bounded worker
record compressed-input/decrypted-output ratios for diagnostics without using them as the primary bound
composition.composition_explanation: The post-allocation size check is one misplaced resource boundary.

source_refs.note: provider returns a complete Vec; software path decompresses then calls as_data_vec; size check follows

notes: Specific to OpenPgpSecretKeyProviderKind::Software. GnuPG and YubiKey providers bound subprocess stdout during read.

title: Conversation queues emit attacker-controlled Unicode bidi controls
root_cause_class: draw_queue formats participant and subject strings directly into Ratatui spans while the reader and HTML renderer use explicit bidi/control sanitizers
demonstrated_impact: An ingested subject containing U+202E reached the real Crossterm writer as UTF-8 E2 80 AE (terminal_contains_rlo=true), permitting row reordering on bidi-capable terminals. The reader neutralizes the same character, so the queue is a policy bypass.
impact_tier_reason: The primitive can distort sender/subject/state presentation on bidi-capable terminals but does not mutate trust state or execute terminal commands. Cold mail remains visibly blue and the reader is sanitized; terminals without bidi support do not reorder it.
exploit_execution_time_source: The UI capture itself completes below the retained command's one-second resolution after compilation.
regression_test_or_invariant: Every attacker-controlled queue field passes through one bidi/control sanitizer before width calculation; captured Crossterm output contains none of U+202A-U+202E or U+2066-U+2069 and contains no active C0/OSC sequence.

unintended_behaviors.behavior: the queue bypasses the inert-text sanitizer used by other message presentation paths
unintended_behaviors.expected: attacker-controlled identity and subject text cannot alter terminal bidi state
unintended_behaviors.actual: participant and subject strings are written directly to terminal spans with bidi formatting characters intact

composition.unintended_behavior_count_note: Sanitizing queue fields before truncation closes the demonstrated path.
remediation_components: shared terminal presentation sanitizer for queue participants and subjects
composition.remediation_component_count_note: No parser or trust-model change is required.
defense_in_depth: render visible bidi-control mnemonics instead of silently dropping them
test combining and zero-width format characters across every screen
composition.composition_explanation: One missing presentation call creates the inconsistency.

source_refs.note: queue emits raw strings while the reader sanitizer covers bidi controls
HTML renderer converts bidi controls to visible mnemonics

notes: Direct OSC 52 injection was rejected: Ratatui removed ESC and BEL. This finding is terminal-dependent UI integrity, not arbitrary terminal control execution.
